article_content: Julle moet julle dus nie bekommer en vra: “Wat moet ons eet of wat moet ons drink of wat moet ons aantrek?” nie. Dit is alles dinge waaroor die ongelowiges begaan is. Julle hemelse Vader weet tog dat julle dit alles nodig het, en Hy sal jul nodige verskaf, selfs as julle nie eens bid nie. (Matteus 6:31-32) Dit klink amper te goed om waar te wees: Jesus sê ons moet ons nie bekommer nie want God weet immers wat ons nodig het, en Hy sal ons altyd verskaf. Om ons totale afhanklikheid van God te bely is nie altyd maklik nie, maar ons moet ons tot die besef kom dat ons Hom bitter nodig het. Jesus beklemtoon: Geseënd is hulle wat weet hoe afhanklik hulle van God is. Nie: Geseënd is hulle wat finansieel sterk staan of met wie dit altyd goed gaan nie, nee: Geseënd is hulle wat weet hoe afhanklik hulle van God is. As brose mense kan ons nie anders as om God geheel en al in alle omstandighede te vertrou nie. Jesus vra: Wie kan deur hulle te bekommer hulle lewe met een enkele uur verleng? Bekommernis is nie ’n las wat God ons opgelê het nie – het jy geweet dat kommer uiters nadelige gevolge op jou liggaam het? Dit breek die liggaam af, want dit lei daartoe dat ’n mens nie kan eet (of te veel eet) of slaap nie; dit neem jou gedagtes oor en belemmer jou vermoë om produktief te wees. Terloops, medici het tot die gevolgtrekking gekom dat die “streshormoon” kortisol, wat ons liggaam afskei wanneer ons ons bekommer, ons gewig laat optel – genoeg rede om nou dadelik op te hou met stres!
translated_content: You should not worry and ask, 'What will we eat or what will we drink or what will we wear?' These are things that unbelievers are concerned about. Your heavenly Father knows that you need them, and He will provide for you, even if you don't pray. (Matthew 6:31-32) It sounds almost too good to be true: Jesus says we shouldn't worry because God knows what we need, and He will always provide. Admitting our total dependence on God is not always easy, but we must come to the realization that we desperately need Him. Jesus emphasizes: Blessed are those who know how dependent they are on God. Not: Blessed are those who are financially strong or who always have it good, no: Blessed are those who know how dependent they are on God. As fragile humans, we cannot help but trust God completely in all circumstances. Jesus asks: Who can extend their life by one hour by worrying? Worrying is not a burden that God has placed on us – did you know that worry has extremely negative consequences on your body? It breaks down the body, because it leads to not being able to eat (or eating too much) or sleep; it takes over your thoughts and hinders your ability to be productive. Worrying can cripple you; it's like a rocking chair: it keeps you busy but gets you nowhere. Give God the first place in your life, turn your worries into prayers, and trust Him for the right outcome. Don't let material things and other needs and desires dominate your life and take the most important place in your life. Experts estimate that 99% of what we worry about will never happen to us. Meanwhile, doctors have come to the conclusion that the 'stress hormone' cortisol, which our body secretes when we worry, causes us to gain weight – enough reason to stop stressing immediately!
